subject: BrightHarbor POC: cost verification & preflight checklist
messages:
From: Sami Reed <sami.reed@brightharbor.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Julia Park <julia.park@brightharbor.com>, procurement@brightharbor.com
Date: 2028-02-28T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Cost validation for POC — workload and assumptions

Sergio,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're excited to move the POC forward. Before we lock dates, procurement and engineering need a short mutual action checklist that validates the cost assumptions (tokens / $) and the operational levers (caching, batching, model variants). To make sure both teams run aligned sims, could you confirm the minimal inputs you need from our side and what Redwood will run?

Attached is our current usage forecast (rough): brightharbor-usage-forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet). Key callouts:
- Primary flow: patient intake + triage (average 260 tokens prompt, 420 tokens response)
- Secondary flow: long-form summarization (avg 1,600 tokens per call)
- Expected concurrency: peak 1200 rps, steady 240 rps (we understand these are high-level)

Procurement wants a one-pager showing: units/$ assumptions per model variant, billing implications for burst windows, and recommended gating criteria for acceptance (target cost per MAU / token). Engineering wants the Redwood sim spec so we can run our own traffic sample.

Can your team provide a short evaluation plan + milestone dates (e.g., baseline sim, caching trial, batching stress) so we can align internal reviewers? Ideally we want to finish verification and sign an initial reserved capacity by mid-March.

Thanks,
Sami Reed
Head of Platform
BrightHarbor

Attachment: brightharbor-usage-forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet, 24KB)

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Sami Reed <sami.reed@brightharbor.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-28T14:32:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Cost validation for POC — workload and assumptions

Sami — great to get that forecast, thanks. Below is a concise evaluation plan we can execute jointly. I kept milestones tight so we can meet your mid-March target.

High-level asks from BrightHarbor (what we need from you):
- Confirm a 72-hour sample of representative request traces (anonymized) or the traffic histogram by endpoint (percentiles for prompt/response tokens).
- Identify two canonical prompt types (short triage, long summarization) in sample form.
- Confirm acceptable latency SLOs per flow (p95 target).

Redwood deliverables (what we'll run and share):
1) Baseline token accounting: per-call token distribution, tokens per end-to-end transaction, and tokens per API unit for each model variant (we'll show tokens/$ at current hosted pricing and an adjusted reserved-capacity estimate).
2) Caching experiment: prefix hit-rate projection and estimated cost delta assuming a 12- to 24-hour session warm cache and prefetch hints.
3) Batching sensitivity: run sims at batching windows of 10ms, 50ms, and 150ms (we'll show latency vs. unit-cost tradeoffs).
4) Model variant comparison: run the above for 3 configurations (baseline open model, quantized variant, and a smaller low-latency model).
5) Acceptance criteria proposal: target tokens/$ < X (we'll compute) and less than 5% degradation in long-form summary quality vs. baseline.

Proposed milestones and timeline (two-week window):
- Mar 1: BrightHarbor provides sample histogram + canonical prompts.
- Mar 3: Redwood shares sim spec and the results template (we'll attach redwood-sim-spec.md and results CSV).
- Mar 6–7: Redwood runs baseline sims and shares initial tokens/$ breakdown.
- Mar 9: Joint review call to reconcile sims and agree acceptance gates.

Notes/assumptions:
- We'll use your forecast numbers but run sensitivity scans +/- 50% in traffic.
- For reserved-capacity pricing tiers, we'll show per-token effective cost under steady vs. burst modes.

I'll loop in engineering (Hannah) and pricing (Karthik/Ben) for the technical and commercial splits. If the dates above work, we'll schedule the review demo for Mar 9.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-sim-spec.md (plain text, 6KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sami Reed <sami.reed@brightharbor.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T09:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cost validation for POC — workload and assumptions

Sami — quick technical notes to make the sims directly comparable:

1) Sampling & token accounting
- Please include both raw token counts and post-tokenization counts (we'll validate tokenizer differences across model variants).

2) Caching profile
- If any of your flows re-use stable prefixes (e.g., intake metadata + repeated clarifying Qs), mark them in the sample. That lets us estimate cache hit-rate conservatively.

3) Batching window choices
- We'll run three windows: immediate (<10ms), mid-window (50–100ms), and relaxed (150ms). For each window we'll report p50/p95 latency and effective tokens per GPU-second. The goal is to expose the inflection point where batching reduces unit cost while still meeting your p95 targets.

4) Prefetch / KV hints
- If you can annotate flows where prefetching context makes sense (sessions likely to continue), we can include a prefetch trial (small, targeted warm cache) — this is often the largest lever for triage flows.

I'll drop the sim spec in the Drive folder as a canonical doc. Sergio — happy to run the baseline once Sami uploads the histogram.

Hannah Schmitt
Staff Engineer, Inference
Redwood Inference

From: Sami Reed <sami.reed@brightharbor.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightharbor.com, Julia Park <julia.park@brightharbor.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T11:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cost validation for POC — workload and assumptions

Thanks, Sergio and Hannah — that plan is exactly what procurement wanted to see. We'll:
- Deliver a 72-hour anonymized histogram and two canonical prompt samples by end of day Mar 1.
- Procurement asks whether Redwood can summarize the billing impact for both hosted (usage) and reserved (committed) modes in the one-pager. If you can show a conservative monthly spend band for steady vs. 3x burst, that will speed approvals.

One additional ask: can Redwood run a small baseline sim against our anonymized traces (no customer data) and post the raw results CSV back to the Drive folder? We'll compare against our internal sim and recon any tokenizer differences.

I'll aim to get the samples to you today.

— Sami
Sami Reed
Head of Platform
BrightHarbor

Attachment: (none)

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Sami Reed <sami.reed@brightharbor.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, procurement@brightharbor.com
Date: 2028-03-02T16:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cost validation for POC — workload and assumptions (next steps)

Sami — confirmed. Next steps and owners: 

- By EOD Mar 1 (BrightHarbor): upload 72-hour anonymized histograms + 2 canonical prompts to the shared Drive. (owner: BrightHarbor)
- By Mar 3 (Redwood): we will publish the sim spec and results template to the Drive (attachments included: redwood-sim-spec.md, redwood-sim-results-template.csv). Pricing (Ben/Karthik): we'll produce a one-pager with units/$ bands for hosted vs. committed tiers and run three burst scenarios (steady, 2x, 3x).
- Mar 6: Redwood runs baseline sims (tokens/$ breakdown) and posts raw CSV. (owner: Redwood engineering)
- Mar 9: Joint review (30–45m) to reconcile sims, finalize acceptance gates, and align reserved capacity start date if the numbers look reasonable.

Quick clarifications:
- Acceptance gate: we'll propose a rolling definition (e.g., 90% of sampled calls fall under target cost band) rather than a single-point metric — this helps account for long-tail summarization traffic.
- Data handling: we will only ingest anonymized histograms and sampled prompts; no customer PII will be uploaded. We'll sign an NDA addendum if needed.

I'll create the Drive folder link and the HubSpot record (HUBSPOT-98765) and drop the sim artifacts there. Tentative deal id: BH-2028-042.

Thanks — see you on the 9th if nothing blocks.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-sim-results-template.csv (CSV template, 2KB)
